intent.raw_query: Greece under $2000, beaches and local food, summer 2026, flying from NYC

selected_hotel.name: Navagio Beach, Zakynthos Island Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Navagio Beach (Shipwreck Beach) Visit
experiences.description: Take a boat tour to the iconic Navagio Beach on Zakynthos, one of Greece's most photographed beaches. The stunning turquoise waters, dramatic limestone cliffs, and the famous shipwreck make this an unmissable experience. Boats depart regularly from Porto Vromi or Zakynthos Town.

experiences.name: Athens Central Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the vibrant Varvakios Agora (Athens Central Market) and surrounding streets. Sample local cheeses, olives, cured meats, fresh seafood, and traditional street foods like spanakopita and loukoumades. Engage with local vendors and discover authentic Greek flavors that tourists rarely experience.

experiences.name: Elafonissi Beach Day Trip
experiences.description: Visit the breathtaking Elafonissi Beach in southwestern Crete, famous for its pink-tinged sand and shallow crystal-clear lagoon. Wade through the warm, knee-deep waters to reach the small island. The unique pink sand comes from crushed shells and coral, making it one of Europe's most unique beaches.

experiences.name: Traditional Cretan Cooking Class
experiences.description: Join a hands-on cooking class in a local Cretan home or taverna and learn to prepare authentic dishes like dakos (barley rusk salad), lamb with stamnagathi (wild greens), and homemade baklava. Includes a visit to a local market to source fresh ingredients and a full sit-down meal with local wine.

experiences.name: Sunset Taverna Dinner in Oia
experiences.description: Experience the world-famous Santorini sunset from the village of Oia while dining at a cliffside taverna. Enjoy fresh grilled octopus, fava (yellow split pea dip), tomatokeftedes (tomato fritters), and local Assyrtiko white wine as the sun dips below the caldera. Book a table in advance for the best views.

weather.summary: Hot and sunny. Sea warm enough for swimming.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Greece
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Navagio Beach, Zakynthos Island Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00. Rest and prepare for travel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Athens International Airport at 13:00. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take the X96 express bus (€6) to Piraeus port. Board the afternoon/evening ferry to Zakynthos (Zante) — journey approx. 6–7 hours. Relax on deck and enjoy the Ionian Sea views.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Zakynthos Town port. Take a local bus or shared taxi to your accommodation near Navagio Beach area. Check in to the Boutique Stay, freshen up, and take a short stroll around the local village to get oriented.

meals.breakfast: Eat before landing or grab a snack at the airport — a tyropita (cheese pie) from a bakery kiosk costs around €1.50
meals.lunch: Grab a souvlaki wrap at Piraeus port area — budget around €3–4 from a street kiosk before boarding
meals.dinner: Simple taverna dinner near your accommodation — try grilled sardines and village salad (horiatiki). Budget €8–10 per person

day_by_day.notes: Book your Piraeus–Zakynthos ferry in advance online (e.g., Anek Lines or Levante Ferries) to save money. A deck-class ticket costs around €20–28. Keep snacks and water handy for the ferry crossing.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast, head down to the famous Navagio Beach (Shipwreck Beach). The only access is by boat — join a shared boat tour from Porto Vromi (the nearest launching point, about 10 min drive). A shared boat trip costs around €10–15 per person. Swim in the stunning turquoise waters beside the rusting shipwreck MV Panagiotis and explore the enclosed limestone cliffs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return from Navagio and walk up to the Navagio Viewpoint (free, accessible by road) for dramatic panoramic photos of the beach from above. The viewpoint is fenced and spectacular — one of Greece's most iconic vistas. Spend time relaxing and photographing.
day_by_day.evening: Head back to the village. Explore the local area on foot, browse small shops selling local olive oil and honey. Watch the sunset from a clifftop vantage point near the accommodation.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the boutique stay or pick up fresh bread, local honey, and yogurt from a nearby mini-market — under €4
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic for Navagio Beach — grab a spanakopita (spinach pie) and fruit from a local bakery — around €3–5
meals.dinner: Dinner at a local taverna in the village — try slow-cooked lamb kleftiko or stuffed tomatoes (gemista) with a carafe of house wine. Budget €10–13 per person

day_by_day.notes: Arrive at Porto Vromi early (before 10:00) to beat the crowds at Navagio Beach. Bring reef-safe sunscreen, a hat, and plenty of water — shade is very limited on the beach. The viewpoint is free and just a short drive or taxi ride from most accommodations in the area.

day_by_day.morning: Take a local bus or rent a scooter (around €15–20/day) and head to the Blue Caves on the northern tip of Zakynthos near Cape Skinari. Join a small rowing boat tour (€10–12) that takes you into the sea caves where the water glows electric blue due to light refraction. Swim in the cave entrances if conditions allow.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue along the northern coast to the village of Volimes — the island's craft village famous for handmade textiles, local honey, and ceramics. Browse the roadside stalls and pick up affordable local souvenirs. Stop at a local honey producer for free tastings.
day_by_day.evening: Return south and stop at the village of Anafonitria to see the medieval Monastery of Anafonitria (free entry, modest dress required) — one of the oldest monasteries on the island with beautiful frescoes. Head back to accommodation and relax.

meals.breakfast: Greek yogurt with local thyme honey and walnuts from the mini-market — €3–4
meals.lunch: Eat at a simple kafeneio (traditional Greek café) in Volimes — try mezes (small plates) like tzatziki, olives, and bread — €6–8
meals.dinner: Cook a simple meal back at accommodation using local market ingredients (fresh vegetables, feta, olives, bread) — under €5, or grab a gyros wrap from a local spot for €3–4

day_by_day.notes: Scooter rental is the most cost-effective and flexible way to explore Zakynthos independently. Always wear a helmet and carry your passport/ID. The Blue Caves are best visited in the morning when sunlight creates the most vivid blue glow in the water.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Laganas Bay on the southern coast — home to one of the most important loggerhead sea turtle (Caretta caretta) nesting sites in the Mediterranean. Visit the National Marine Park of Zakynthos information center (free) to learn about turtle conservation. Walk along the quieter end of Laganas Beach in the morning before crowds arrive.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to nearby Kalamaki Beach — slightly less touristy than Laganas, with calm clear water perfect for swimming. Rent a sunbed (€4–6 for two) or simply lay your towel on the free public beach section. Snorkel along the rocky edges — good chance of spotting sea turtles naturally.
day_by_day.evening: Head into Zakynthos Town (Zante Town) for the evening. Stroll the Venetian-influenced waterfront (Bochali area), visit the free-entry ruins of Zakynthos Castle at dusk for panoramic views over the town and bay.

meals.breakfast: Grab a koulouri (sesame bread ring) and a freddo cappuccino at a local café — €2–3
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood at a casual taverna near Kalamaki Beach — grilled octopus or calamari with chips and salad — €10–12
meals.dinner: Dinner in Zakynthos Town — try a traditional restaurant serving bourdeto (spicy fish stew, a local Zakynthian specialty) with local bread — €10–13 per person

day_by_day.notes: Do not disturb sea turtle nests marked on Laganas Beach — they are protected by law. Avoid visiting the beach at night during nesting season (May–October). Zakynthos Town is about 35–40 minutes from Navagio area by scooter or bus.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Zakynthos Town properly — visit the Museum of Solomos and Eminent Zakynthians (€3 entry), dedicated to Dionysios Solomos, who wrote the Greek national anthem. Walk through the elegant Plateia Agiou Markou (Saint Mark's Square) and admire the Venetian-style architecture reconstructed after the 1953 earthquake.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Byzantine Museum of Zakynthos on the main square (€3 entry) housing an impressive collection of post-Byzantine icons and religious art rescued from earthquake-damaged churches. Afterward, walk to the waterfront and browse the local market stalls for fresh produce, spices, and local products.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Navagio area. Enjoy a slow sunset evening — find a clifftop spot with a cold Mythos beer from a mini-market (€1.50) and watch the sun set over the Ionian Sea. Early night to rest.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a traditional Zakynthian café in town — try mandolato (local nougat) and Greek coffee — €3–4
meals.lunch: Street food lunch in Zakynthos Town — souvlaki skewer with pita, tomato, onion, and tzatziki — €2.50–3.50 each
meals.dinner: Cook at accommodation or pick up fresh local produce from the town market — make a simple Greek salad, feta, olives, and fresh bread — under €6

day_by_day.notes: Most museums in Zakynthos Town are closed on Mondays — check opening days before visiting. The town waterfront is lovely for an evening walk with affordable café seating. Stock up on local products like Zakynthian olive oil and mandolato as gifts — excellent value at local shops.

day_by_day.morning: Full relaxation morning at Navagio Beach or Porto Vromi Beach (closer and free to access by land). Swim, snorkel, and soak up the sun. The sea temperature in June is around 23–24°C — perfect for extended swimming. Bring your own snorkel gear if possible (or rent from a beach shop for €5).
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike the trail from the Navagio viewpoint area along the clifftops — a scenic and free walk with extraordinary views of the coastline. The trail is rugged so wear proper shoes. Explore hidden coves accessible on foot along the northern cliffs.
day_by_day.evening: Visit a local olive oil producer or winery in the Volimes/Katastari area for an informal tasting (many offer free or very low-cost tastings). Pick up a bottle of local wine (€4–6) for the evening. Enjoy a relaxed dinner back near your accommodation.

meals.breakfast: Greek yogurt parfait with local honey, nuts, and seasonal fruit — self-prepared, under €4
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch to enjoy on the clifftop trail — local cheese (graviera), olives, bread, and cherry tomatoes — €4–5 from mini-market
meals.dinner: Taverna dinner near Navagio — try pastitsada (pasta with meat sauce) or sofrito (veal in white wine sauce) — €9–12 per person

day_by_day.notes: This is a good rest and recharge day before preparing for travel to the next destination. The cliff hike is best done in the early afternoon once the tour boats have left Navagio, giving you quieter viewpoint access. Always carry water on hikes — heat can be intense at 29°C.

day_by_day.morning: Check out of the Navagio accommodation. Pack bags and take the ferry from Zakynthos Port back to Killini on the Peloponnese mainland (approx. 1 hour, around €8–10). From Killini, take a bus to Patras (approx. 1 hour, €4) and then a KTEL bus to Athens (approx. 3 hours, €18–20).
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Athens. Check in to a budget hostel or guesthouse in the Monastiraki or Psiri neighborhood (dorms from €15–20/night, private rooms from €35–50). Drop bags and head immediately to explore the atmospheric Monastiraki Flea Market — a maze of antiques, vintage clothing, street food, and local crafts.
day_by_day.evening: Walk to the Acropolis Hill area and enjoy the free view of the illuminated Parthenon from Areopagus Hill (Mars Hill) — a flat rocky outcrop just below the Acropolis with stunning panoramic views of Athens at dusk. No entry fee required.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast before departure — bread with local honey and instant coffee at accommodation — under €3
meals.lunch: Eat on the ferry or grab a snack at Patras bus station — a tiropita or spanakopita — €2–3
meals.dinner: Dinner in Monastiraki — try a classic souvlaki at Thanasis or Kostas (legendary local spots) — a full meal with pita, meat, and drink for €6–8

day_by_day.notes: Book the KTEL bus from Patras to Athens in advance at ktelbus.com to guarantee a seat, especially in peak June season. Store luggage at Athens airport or bus station lockers if needed. The Monastiraki area is ideal for budget travelers — central, lively, and full of affordable food options.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Acropolis of Athens (€20 entry, or €30 for a combined ticket covering 7 major archaeological sites — excellent value). Arrive early (opens at 8:00) to beat the heat and crowds. Explore the Parthenon, Erechtheion, Propylaea, and the Temple of Athena Nike. Allow 2–2.5 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head down to the Acropolis Museum (€10 entry) — one of Europe's finest modern museums, housing original sculptures and artifacts from the Acropolis in stunning glass-and-concrete architecture. Spend 1.5–2 hours exploring. Afterward, walk through the charming Plaka neighborhood — Athens' oldest district with neoclassical houses, bougainvillea, and craft shops.
day_by_day.evening: Climb Lycabettus Hill for the best panoramic sunset view over Athens (free on foot, or funicular €7 return). Watch the city light up as the sun sets behind the Acropolis. Head back down for dinner in the lively Exarcheia or Psiri neighborhood.

meals.breakfast: Traditional Greek breakfast at a local café — freddo espresso, koulouri, and a cheese pie — €3–4
meals.lunch: Lunch in Plaka — try a traditional taverna set menu (fixed-price lunch menus often €8–11 including a main, salad, and bread)
meals.dinner: Dinner in Psiri neighborhood — mezedes (shared small plates) at a casual ouzeri — dolmades, taramosalata, grilled halloumi, and ouzo — €10–13 per person

day_by_day.notes: The combined 7-site ticket (€30) is valid for 5 days and covers the Acropolis, Ancient Agora, Roman Agora, Kerameikos, Temple of Olympian Zeus, Hadrian's Library, and the Lykeion — excellent value if you plan to visit multiple sites. Book Acropolis tickets online to skip queues.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Ancient Agora of Athens (included in combined ticket) — the heart of ancient Athenian civic life. Walk among the ruins and visit the remarkably well-preserved Temple of Hephaestus. Explore the Stoa of Attalos museum inside. Allow 1.5–2 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take Metro Line 1 to Piraeus (€1.20) and spend the afternoon exploring the lively Mikrolimano harbor — a picturesque circular harbor filled with fishing boats and seafood restaurants. Walk along the waterfront, browse the Central Fish Market, and enjoy the authentic port atmosphere away from tourist crowds.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Athens and explore the Kerameikos archaeological site (combined ticket) — the ancient cemetery district with fascinating funerary monuments, less visited than the Acropolis but equally atmospheric. End the evening with a walk through Gazi neighborhood — Athens' trendy arts and nightlife district.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a local bakery near the hostel — fresh tiropita, loukoumades (honey doughnuts), and Greek coffee — €3–5
meals.lunch: Fresh grilled fish lunch at a simple psarotaverna (fish taverna) at Mikrolimano — grilled sea bream with lemon, olive oil, and salad — €12–15 (splurge-worthy for freshness)
meals.dinner: Budget dinner in Gazi — a large gyros plate with fries and tzatziki — €5–7, or falafel wrap at a street food spot

day_by_day.notes: Piraeus and Mikrolimano are authentic, local experiences rarely covered in tourist guides. The fish market is most active in the morning but the harbor is lovely all day. Avoid the tourist-trap restaurants directly on the main Piraeus waterfront — walk around to Mikrolimano for better quality and value.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Cape Sounion (about 70 km from Athens). Catch the KTEL bus from Pedion Areos bus terminal (€6.50 each way, approx. 2 hours). Visit the Temple of Poseidon at Cape Sounion (€8 entry) — a stunning clifftop temple dramatically perched 60 meters above the Aegean Sea, where Lord Byron famously carved his name into a column.
day_by_day.afternoon: Swim at the small beach directly below the temple headland — the water is crystal clear and the setting is extraordinary. Relax, snorkel, and enjoy the relative quiet compared to main Athens beaches. The bus back to Athens departs in the late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Athens by early evening. Explore the Central Athens Food Market (Varvakios Agora) on Athinas Street — even if winding down for the day, the area around it is full of affordable local tavernas and ouzeris. Enjoy a relaxed final Athens evening.

meals.breakfast: Self-prepared breakfast at hostel — bread, local feta, tomatoes, olives — €3–4
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic for Cape Sounion — local cheese, bread, fruit, and water from a supermarket — €4–5, or eat at the simple café at the site (budget €8–10)
meals.dinner: Dinner near Varvakios market area — try a traditional psistaria (grill house) with grilled lamb chops (paidakia), tzatziki, and pita bread — €12–15 per person

day_by_day.notes: The KTEL bus to Cape Sounion departs roughly every hour from the terminal near Pedion Areos park. Check the return schedule carefully as buses become less frequent in the late afternoon. Bring swimming gear, sunscreen, and a hat — there is limited shade at the temple and beach.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Athens Metro to Piraeus port and catch a fast ferry or hydrofoil to the island of Aegina (approx. 40 minutes, €8–12 return on a day-trip ticket). Arrive and rent a bicycle (€5–8/day) or take a local bus to the magnificent Temple of Aphaia (€6 entry) — one of the best-preserved ancient temples in Greece with a stunning hilltop setting.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cycle or bus to Aegina Town beach for a swim. The island is famous for its pistachios — buy a fresh bag directly from roadside producers (€3–5 for 200g) — the best pistachios in Greece. Explore the charming neoclassical waterfront of Aegina Town with its colorful fishing boats and horse-drawn carriages.
day_by_day.evening: Take the ferry back to Piraeus and return to Athens by Metro. Enjoy a final evening in Athens — walk through Monastiraki and Thissio neighborhoods and enjoy a drink at a rooftop bar with Acropolis views (many offer happy hour deals — a beer or wine for €4–6).

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast at Piraeus port — a spanakopita and freddo cappuccino from a port-side bakery — €3–4
meals.lunch: Fresh fish lunch at a simple taverna on Aegina waterfront — grilled red mullet (barbounia) with lemon and olive oil — €10–13
meals.dinner: Light dinner in Monastiraki — a large Greek salad, hummus, and pita at a casual spot — €7–9

day_by_day.notes: Aegina makes a perfect, affordable day trip from Athens — far less crowded than Santorini or Mykonos but equally charming. The Aegina pistachios are genuinely world-class — buy directly from producers rather than shops for the best price. Ferries run frequently throughout the day from Piraeus Gate E8/E9.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the National Archaeological Museum of Athens (€12 entry, free on first Sunday of the month) — the largest archaeological museum in Greece and one of the most important in the world. Home to the Antikythera Mechanism, Mask of Agamemnon, and extraordinary ancient Greek sculptures. Allow 2.5–3 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the vibrant Exarcheia neighborhood — Athens' bohemian, alternative district full of independent bookshops, street art murals, small cafés, and local character. Visit the small Strefi Hill park for a free city view without the tourist crowds. Browse the weekly street market if running (check local listings).
day_by_day.evening: Final Athens evening — take a leisurely walk along the Dionysiou Areopagitou pedestrian promenade that runs below the Acropolis, connecting Monastiraki to Thissio and Koukaki. Lined with cafés, street performers, and stunning lit-up views of the Acropolis. Perfect for a final atmospheric stroll and dinner.

meals.breakfast: Traditional Greek breakfast at a neighborhood café — Greek coffee, fresh orange juice, and a toast with local honey — €4–5
meals.lunch: Lunch in Exarcheia — try a local workers' restaurant (estiatorio) offering daily specials like moussaka, pastitsio, or yemista — full meal for €7–9
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner on the Dionysiou Areopagitou promenade area — splurge slightly on a rooftop restaurant with Acropolis views — grilled octopus, fresh bread, wine — €18–22 per person (treat yourself!)

day_by_day.notes: The National Archaeological Museum is slightly off the main tourist trail but absolutely unmissable — budget at least 2.5 hours. The Dionysiou Areopagitou promenade is one of the most beautiful urban walks in Europe and completely free. It connects seamlessly to the Ancient Agora area.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Athens — wake up early and visit the Monastiraki Flea Market one last time for any last-minute souvenirs (best selection on Sunday mornings, but open daily). Pick up affordable gifts: evil eye amulets (mati), local herbs and spices, small ceramic pieces, or local honey and olive oil products — all at very reasonable prices.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight time, visit the Roman Agora and Hadrian's Library (combined ticket) — both just a short walk from Monastiraki and often overlooked by visitors. The Tower of the Winds (Aerides) inside is particularly impressive. Head to the airport with plenty of time — take the Metro X3 line directly to Athens International Airport (€9, approx. 40 minutes from city center).
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Athens International Airport. Reflect on 13 incredible days exploring Greece's beaches, ancient history, and extraordinary local food culture.

meals.breakfast: Final Greek breakfast — a full spread at a café near Monastiraki: Greek coffee, fresh orange juice, tiropita, and loukoumades with honey and cinnamon — €5–7 (treat yourself for the last morning!)
meals.lunch: Light lunch near the airport or a final souvlaki wrap in the city before heading to the airport — €4–6
meals.dinner: Airport meal or on-board flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for the Metro journey and airport check-in/security. The Athens Metro to the airport runs every 30 minutes and is by far the most affordable and reliable airport transfer option. Pack any local food products (olive oil, honey, herbs) in checked luggage to avoid security issues. Total estimated budget for the full 13 days (excluding flights): approximately €500–650 per person, including accommodation, transport, food, and entrance fees.

trip_options.title: Classic Greece Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Navagio Beach, Zakynthos Island Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Collect luggage and arrange transfer.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer from airport to Navagio Beach boutique stay (approx. 1.5–2 hrs including ferry if needed). Check in, freshen up, and take a slow stroll along the nearest accessible coastal path to get your bearings. Enjoy the first views of the Ionian Sea from your accommodation.
day_by_day.evening: Easy first evening — explore the immediate village area on foot. Watch the sunset over the Ionian Sea from a nearby clifftop or terrace viewpoint near Navagio.

meals.breakfast: Grab a snack or coffee at the airport before or after landing.
meals.lunch: Light bite at a small kafeneion (traditional Greek café) near the port or on the transfer route — try a tyropita (cheese pie) and Greek coffee.
meals.dinner: Dinner at a relaxed taverna near your boutique stay — order fresh grilled fish of the day, a Greek salad with local feta, and a carafe of house white wine. Budget approx. €20–28 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 low-key to recover from travel. Confirm with your accommodation any ferry or road transfer logistics in advance. Exchange some cash for smaller local tavernas that may not accept cards.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the iconic Navagio Beach (Shipwreck Beach) — take the short boat trip from the nearby port (boats depart regularly in summer, approx. €15–20 round trip). Arrive early to beat the midday crowds. Swim in the crystal-clear turquoise water and explore the famous rusting shipwreck MV Panagiotis on the white pebble beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Relax on Navagio Beach through the early afternoon — the water is warm and the limestone cliffs provide dramatic scenery. Return by boat around 14:30–15:00. Back at the hotel, rest during the hottest part of the day (peak heat ~29°C).
day_by_day.evening: Head into the nearby village of Anafonitria or Volimes for a gentle evening walk. Browse local shops selling Zakynthian honey, olive oil, and handmade goods.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your boutique stay or a nearby café — Greek yogurt with thyme honey and walnuts, fresh bread, and a freddo espresso.
meals.lunch: Pack a simple picnic to enjoy on Navagio Beach — grab fresh bread, local olives, cheese, and fruit from a small market before boarding the boat.
meals.dinner: Dinner at a village taverna in Anafonitria — try sofrito (Zakynthian veal in white wine and garlic sauce) or pastitsada, paired with local Zakynthian wine. Budget approx. €22–30 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Boat trips to Navagio can sell out in peak season — book the morning slot the evening before or ask your accommodation to arrange it. Wear water shoes as the beach is pebbly. Apply strong sunscreen; the beach has no shade.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Blue Caves (Kyanoun Spileon) on the northern tip of Zakynthos — take a boat tour from Porto Vromi or Agios Nikolaos port (approx. €20–25). The caves glow with vivid blue light in the morning when the sun angle is perfect. Swim inside the cave entrances.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return from the caves and visit Porto Vromi beach — a quiet, sheltered cove perfect for snorkeling. The water is exceptionally clear with good marine life visibility. Bring or rent a snorkel set (available at the port, approx. €5).
day_by_day.evening: Return to your accommodation to shower and change. Drive or take a taxi to the village of Volimes — the largest village in northern Zakynthos — for an evening browse of artisan shops and a quiet drink at a local café.

meals.breakfast: At your boutique stay — scrambled eggs, village bread with local olive oil and oregano, fresh orange juice.
meals.lunch: Seafood lunch at a small harbour-side taverna near Porto Vromi — grilled octopus, calamari, and a cold Mythos beer. Budget approx. €15–20 per person.
meals.dinner: Back near your accommodation — try a different local taverna and order mandoles (Zakynthian almond pralines) for dessert, a regional specialty. Main course: moussaka or stuffed tomatoes. Budget approx. €18–25 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Blue Caves boat tours are best in the morning (before 11:00) for optimal light. Confirm departure point with your accommodation — Porto Vromi is closest to Navagio area. Bring a waterproof bag for your phone and valuables on the boat.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a scooter or car for the day (available in Volimes or Zakynthos Town area, approx. €30–45/day for a scooter). Drive south along the scenic west coast road, stopping at the clifftop viewpoint above Navagio for the famous panoramic photograph of Shipwreck Beach from above.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue south to Exo Chora and Maries villages — quiet, authentic Zakynthian villages largely untouched by tourism. Walk the shaded village squares, visit a small Byzantine church, and chat with locals. Stop at a roadside stall selling local produce.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Navagio area. Enjoy a relaxed evening at your boutique stay — use any pool or terrace facilities. Watch the golden hour light on the Ionian Sea.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before setting off — Greek honey cake (melomakarona-style pastry), coffee, and yogurt.
meals.lunch: Village taverna lunch in Maries or Exo Chora — simple home-cooked dishes like fasolada (bean soup), horiatiki salad, and fresh bread. Very affordable at approx. €10–14 per person.
meals.dinner: Cook-in evening or order local mezedes (small plates) from a nearby takeaway — olives, tzatziki, spanakopita, and local cheese. Enjoy on your hotel terrace with a bottle of local Robola or Verdea wine (approx. €8–12 from a local shop).

day_by_day.notes: Scooter rental requires a valid driving licence (motorcycle category in most EU countries). Roads in northern Zakynthos can be narrow and winding — drive carefully. Fuel up before heading into the villages as petrol stations are sparse in the north.

day_by_day.morning: Beach day at Xigia Beach — a unique sulphur-spring beach on the northeast coast of Zakynthos (approx. 30-minute drive from Navagio area). The natural sulphur springs bubble up through the seabed, giving the water a silky texture said to be good for the skin. Swim and snorkel in the clear water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive further south to Makris Gialos or Alykanas beach for a change of scenery — a long sandy stretch with calm, shallow water. Rent a sunbed (approx. €5–8) and spend a few hours swimming and relaxing.
day_by_day.evening: Head into Zakynthos Town (Zante Town) for the evening — a 45-minute drive south. Stroll the elegant Venetian-influenced waterfront (Strada Marina), visit Solomos Square, and enjoy the lively atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a quick stop at a bakery en route — koulouria (sesame bread rings) and a hot drink.
meals.lunch: Casual beach taverna at Alykanas — grilled sea bream (tsipoura), Greek salad, and fresh lemonade. Budget approx. €16–22 per person.
meals.dinner: Dinner in Zakynthos Town at a mid-range restaurant on the waterfront — try Zakynthian-style rabbit stifado or fresh lobster pasta. Budget approx. €25–35 per person. Stroll the waterfront with a gelato afterwards.

day_by_day.notes: Xigia Beach has limited parking and no facilities — arrive early and bring your own water and snacks. The sulphur smell is noticeable but not unpleasant. Zakynthos Town is a good opportunity to stock up on any supplies, visit a pharmacy, or use an ATM.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Venetian Castle (Kastro) above Zakynthos Town — an early morning hike or taxi ride up to the hilltop fortress offers sweeping views over the town and bay. Explore the ruins and the pine forest within the castle walls. Cool and shaded in the morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Zakynthos Town on foot — visit the Museum of Solomos and Eminent Zakynthians (dedicated to the poet Dionysios Solomos, author of the Greek national anthem, entry approx. €3), and the Byzantine Museum on Solomos Square with its collection of post-Byzantine icons salvaged from the 1953 earthquake.
day_by_day.evening: Browse the main shopping street (Alexandrou Roma) for local souvenirs — Zakynthian nougat (mandoles), local liqueurs, and olive oil products. Enjoy a final Zakynthos Town dinner before returning to your accommodation.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a café in Zakynthos Town — bougatsa (custard-filled pastry) and a frappe or freddo cappuccino, a classic Greek morning combination.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a traditional ouzeri (ouzo bar with food) in Zakynthos Town — order a selection of mezedes: taramosalata, grilled sardines, dolmades, and a small carafe of ouzo or tsipouro. Budget approx. €14–18 per person.
meals.dinner: Dinner at a taverna in the backstreets of Zakynthos Town away from the tourist waterfront — better value and more authentic. Try bianco (local white fish stew with garlic and lemon) — a signature Zakynthian dish. Budget approx. €20–26 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Venetian Castle is best visited before 10:00 to avoid the heat. Wear comfortable shoes for the cobblestone paths. The Byzantine Museum is air-conditioned — a welcome respite on a hot afternoon. Return to Navagio area by taxi or rental car (keep the car if still rented from Day 4).

day_by_day.morning: Rest and leisure morning at your boutique stay — sleep in, enjoy a slow breakfast, and use the hotel's amenities. This is your mid-trip recovery day. Read by the pool or on a terrace overlooking the sea.
day_by_day.afternoon: Short walk to a quiet, less-visited local cove near Navagio — ask your accommodation for their recommended secret spot. Bring a book, snorkel, and plenty of water. Enjoy a completely private and unhurried afternoon swim.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktail hour at a clifftop bar near Navagio — the west-facing cliffs offer some of the best sunsets in Greece. Order a Aperol Spritz or a local Zakynthian spirit-based cocktail.

meals.breakfast: Indulgent hotel breakfast — full spread with eggs, local cheeses, cured meats, fresh fruit, and pastries. Take your time.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the hotel or from a local deli — fresh bread, hummus, grilled vegetables, and cold cuts. Keep it simple.
meals.dinner: Special dinner at the best-rated taverna near your accommodation — splurge slightly on a seafood platter for two (lobster, prawns, grilled fish, calamari) with a bottle of chilled Assyrtiko white wine. Budget approx. €35–50 per person for this treat.

day_by_day.notes: Day 7 is intentionally relaxed — a balanced itinerary needs breathing room. Use this day to recharge before the second week. Do laundry if needed (ask your accommodation). Check any ferry or transport bookings for the days ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to the south of Zakynthos — drive to Gerakas Beach, a stunning protected loggerhead sea turtle (Caretta caretta) nesting beach in the Vassilikos peninsula. Arrive early (beach opens at 08:00, closes at dusk for turtle protection). Swim in the calm, shallow turquoise water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Porto Zoro Beach — a beautiful, less-crowded sandy beach nearby. Excellent snorkeling along the rocky edges. Alternatively, visit Banana Beach (Agios Nikolaos) for a livelier beach club atmosphere with water sports available.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back north toward Navagio. Stop in Laganas or Argassi for a lively evening if you want a change of pace — these are more tourist-oriented resort towns with a buzzing evening scene.

meals.breakfast: Early departure — grab a coffee and pastry from a roadside bakery or petrol station en route.
meals.lunch: Beach taverna near Gerakas or Porto Zoro — simple grilled chicken souvlaki, tzatziki, pita, and a cold drink. Budget approx. €12–16 per person.
meals.dinner: If staying in the south for the evening: dinner in Argassi with views of the bay and Peloponnese coast in the distance. Try a mixed grill platter. If returning north: a local taverna near Navagio. Budget approx. €18–25 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Gerakas Beach has strict rules — no umbrellas, no ball games, no dogs, and certain zones are roped off for turtle nests. Rangers are present. Respect the rules and enjoy the rare privilege of swimming on an active turtle nesting beach. Best chance of seeing turtle tracks in the sand is early morning.

day_by_day.morning: Morning boat excursion — join a shared boat tour departing from Porto Vromi visiting multiple sea caves, snorkeling spots, and hidden coves along the northern Zakynthos coastline. Many tours include a stop at Navagio from the sea again (different perspective) and the Blue Caves. Approx. €30–40 per person for a half-day shared tour.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return by early afternoon. Spend the hottest hours (13:00–16:00) resting at the hotel or in a shaded café. Read, nap, or enjoy a cold frappe in the shade — embrace the Greek concept of the afternoon rest.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the village of Anafonitria — home to the 15th-century monastery of Agios Dionysios (Anafonitria Monastery), the patron saint of Zakynthos. A peaceful, historic site open to respectful visitors. Dress modestly (shoulders and knees covered).

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — keep it light before the boat trip. Fresh fruit, yogurt, and a small coffee.
meals.lunch: On-board or at the harbour upon return — grilled octopus and a cold beer at a portside café. Budget approx. €12–16 per person.
meals.dinner: Dinner at a family-run taverna in Anafonitria village after visiting the monastery — simple, home-style cooking. Try gemista (stuffed tomatoes and peppers with rice) and a village salad. Very affordable at approx. €14–18 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book the boat tour the previous evening to secure spots — tours fill up quickly in June. Bring reef-safe sunscreen, a hat, and a light cover-up for the monastery visit. The monastery may have specific visiting hours — check locally.

day_by_day.morning: Cooking and food experience morning — visit the weekly local market in Volimes (check current market day with your accommodation) or a nearby village market. Buy fresh local produce: tomatoes, cucumbers, local cheese, herbs, and honey. Engage with vendors and learn about local ingredients.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrange a short olive oil or local food tasting experience — many agritourism farms near Volimes offer informal tastings of olive oil, local wines, and traditional products (often free or a small charge of €5–10). Alternatively, spend the afternoon at a quiet beach of your choice for a final extended swim session.
day_by_day.evening: Prepare a simple self-catered meal using your market purchases, or dine at a taverna with a focus on trying dishes you haven't yet experienced — perhaps skordalia (garlic potato dip), loukoumades (honey doughnuts), or a local cheese board.

meals.breakfast: At the hotel — a leisurely breakfast before heading to the market.
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch assembled from market purchases — fresh bread, local tomatoes drizzled with olive oil and oregano, feta cheese, olives, and seasonal fruit. Eat at a scenic viewpoint or quiet beach.
meals.dinner: Taverna dinner — focus on Zakynthian specialties you haven't tried yet. Order a tasting-style meal with multiple small dishes. Finish with local dessert: revani (semolina cake soaked in syrup) and a small glass of Verdea wine. Budget approx. €20–28 per person.

day_by_day.notes: This day is designed around the local food interest — immerse yourself in the food culture of Zakynthos. Ask your accommodation host for their personal restaurant recommendations; locals always know the best-value, most authentic spots. Verdea is a unique amber-coloured wine made only on Zakynthos — worth trying.

day_by_day.morning: Final full beach day — return to your favourite beach discovered during the trip, or try Sekania Beach (if accessible — it's the most protected turtle nesting beach, sometimes open to guided visits). Alternatively, spend the morning at a quieter stretch near Porto Vromi with calm, deep-blue water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Water sports session — many beaches offer paddleboard rentals (approx. €15/hr), kayak rentals (approx. €10–15/hr), or guided sea kayaking tours along the coast. A sea kayak tour to a nearby sea cave is a memorable way to spend a final active afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell drinks at a clifftop bar watching the sunset. Reflect on the trip over a glass of local wine or a Greek cocktail (try a mastiha-based drink). Golden hour on the Ionian cliffs is unforgettable.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — enjoy it fully as one of your last mornings.
meals.lunch: Beach taverna — keep it light and fresh: grilled fish, salad, and sparkling water or a cold rosé wine.
meals.dinner: Special farewell dinner — return to the best taverna you discovered during the trip, or try a slightly more upscale restaurant for a celebratory final meal. Order the freshest fish available, a bottle of good Greek wine, and save room for dessert. Budget approx. €30–40 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Use this day to begin packing and organizing any souvenirs. Drop off rental car or scooter if still in use. Confirm your departure logistics for the final days. Buy any last local products — olive oil, honey, and mandoles travel well as gifts.

day_by_day.morning: Slow, relaxed final morning at your boutique stay — enjoy the view, have a long breakfast, and soak in the atmosphere of Navagio one last time. Take a final short walk to your favourite coastal viewpoint for a last look at the Ionian Sea.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out and begin transfer toward Zakynthos airport or port (depending on onward travel). If time allows before departure logistics, stop in Zakynthos Town for any last-minute shopping or a final coffee on the waterfront.
day_by_day.evening: Departure evening — if flying out, allow ample time for the airport. If staying an extra night near the airport or port, enjoy a simple dinner in Zakynthos Town.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast — savour every bite of the Greek yogurt, honey, and fresh pastries.
meals.lunch: Light lunch in Zakynthos Town before heading to the airport — a gyros wrap or a souvlaki pita from a street-food spot. Budget approx. €5–8 per person.
meals.dinner: Airport dinner or a final taverna meal near the airport/port — keep it simple: a Greek salad, some mezedes, and a cold drink. Budget approx. €15–20 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Zakynthos Airport (ZTH) is small — allow at least 1.5–2 hours before departure. Traffic in summer can cause delays on the main road to the airport. Confirm your flight time and check-in requirements. Keep some euro coins for airport trolleys or small purchases.

day_by_day.morning: Departure day — if your flight departs in the morning, transfer to Zakynthos Airport with plenty of time. Final views of the Ionian islands from the plane window as you depart. If you have a late flight, enjoy one last leisurely morning in Greece.
day_by_day.afternoon: In-flight or at connecting airport. If a long layover, explore the airport or rest.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive home with memories of turquoise waters, clifftop sunsets, fresh seafood, and the warm hospitality of Zakynthos.

meals.breakfast: Airport café or hotel — final Greek coffee and a pastry before departure.
meals.lunch: Airport or in-flight meal.
meals.dinner: In-flight or at home.

day_by_day.notes: This 13-day itinerary was designed to balance active beach exploration, local food discovery, cultural visits, and genuine relaxation — the essence of a balanced Greek island holiday. Zakynthos, while famous for Navagio, reveals its true character in its villages, hidden coves, and family-run tavernas. Καλό ταξίδι — have a great journey!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Greece Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Navagio Beach, Zakynthos Island Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Zakynthos International Airport at 13:00 – no morning activities scheduled
day_by_day.afternoon: Private transfer from Zakynthos Airport to Navagio Beach Boutique Stay. Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely first stroll along the clifftops overlooking the iconic Shipwreck Beach (Navagio). Sip a welcome cocktail on your private terrace while soaking in the panoramic Ionian Sea views.
day_by_day.evening: Gentle sunset walk along the cliff edge viewpoint above Navagio Beach, one of the most photographed spots in Greece. Watch the golden light illuminate the stranded MV Panagiotis shipwreck below.

meals.breakfast: N/A – in-flight or airport
meals.lunch: Light welcome spread arranged by the boutique hotel upon arrival – local cheeses, Zakynthian cold cuts, olives, and fresh bread with local thyme honey
meals.dinner: Dinner at the hotel's private terrace restaurant or a short drive to Alykes area – try Zakynthian sofrito (veal in white wine and garlic sauce) and fresh grilled sea bream paired with local Verdea white wine

day_by_day.notes: Request an early check-in if possible when booking. The cliff viewpoint above Navagio is accessible by foot from most boutique properties in the area and is magical at golden hour. Unpack and rest – a full adventure begins tomorrow.

day_by_day.morning: Private boat charter departing from the nearby small port – descend to Navagio (Shipwreck) Beach by sea, the only way to access this enclosed cove. Swim in the electric-blue water, explore the rusting shipwreck up close, and enjoy the dramatic limestone cliffs in near-total seclusion during the early hours before day-trippers arrive.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the private boat tour northward along the Zakynthos coastline, stopping at the famous Blue Caves near Cape Skinari. Snorkel through the sea caves where sunlight refracts into dazzling blue hues. Anchor in a secluded bay for a champagne lunch on deck.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the boutique stay and refresh. Drive or arrange a transfer to Volimes village, the traditional hilltop village closest to Navagio, for an authentic evening among locals.

meals.breakfast: Full Greek breakfast at the hotel – Greek yogurt with Zakynthian thyme honey, fresh fruit, spanakopita, eggs, and fresh-squeezed orange juice
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic lunch served on the private boat – smoked salmon, local graviera cheese, marinated octopus, stuffed vine leaves, fresh crusty bread, and chilled rosé wine
meals.dinner: Dinner at a traditional taverna in Volimes village – try bourdeto (spicy fish stew unique to the Ionian islands) and local loukoumades (honey doughnuts) for dessert

day_by_day.notes: Book the private boat charter well in advance – half-day or full-day options available. Depart by 08:00–08:30 to reach Navagio before the tourist crowds arrive by 10:00. Bring reef-safe sunscreen, a hat, and water shoes for the cave exploration.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise yoga or meditation session on the hotel terrace overlooking the Ionian Sea (arrange with the hotel concierge in advance). Follow with a slow, indulgent breakfast. Then set out on a private guided hiking tour along the clifftop trails above Navagio, learning about the island's geology, flora, and the legend of the smuggler ship.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the secluded Porto Limnionas rocky cove on the western coast – a hidden gem with crystal-clear turquoise water carved into dramatic limestone. Swim, snorkel, and relax on the rocks. This spot is far less crowded than main beaches and perfect for a premium, peaceful experience.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner drinks at the Navagio viewpoint – arrive with a bottle of chilled local wine from the hotel and watch the sunset paint the cliffs in shades of amber and rose. One of the most spectacular sunsets in the Mediterranean.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely hotel breakfast with a focus on local Zakynthian products – mandola almond sweets, local honey cake, fresh pastries, and Greek mountain tea
meals.lunch: Seafood lunch at a small family-run spot near Porto Limnionas – fresh catch of the day, grilled octopus, and Greek salad with Zakynthian feta
meals.dinner: Private in-room or terrace dining experience arranged through the boutique hotel – a curated tasting menu of Ionian specialties with wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Porto Limnionas requires a short drive from Navagio area – ask the hotel for directions or arrange a driver. Wear sturdy sandals for the rocky shoreline. The clifftop hike is moderate – takes approximately 2 hours and rewards with multiple breathtaking viewpoints.

day_by_day.morning: Private transfer to Zakynthos Town (Chora) on the eastern coast – approximately 40 minutes from Navagio. Explore the elegant Venetian-influenced town, stroll along the marble-paved waterfront esplanade, and visit the Byzantine Museum housing stunning post-Byzantine icons and frescoes rescued after the 1953 earthquake.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the hilltop Venetian Castle (Kastro) above Zakynthos Town for sweeping views over the bay and the Peloponnese coastline in the distance. Explore the ruined walls and lush pine forest within the castle grounds. Then relax at a premium beach club on the calmer eastern side of the island – try Tsilivi or Planos area for a more upscale beach experience.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Zakynthos Town's elegant waterfront district – one of the best dining scenes on the island with fresh seafood restaurants and wine bars.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Upscale meze lunch at a waterfront restaurant in Zakynthos Town – sharing plates of taramosalata, grilled calamari, saganaki cheese flambéed with ouzo, and fresh bread
meals.dinner: Fine dining at one of Zakynthos Town's top restaurants – try kakavia (traditional fisherman's soup), lobster pasta, and a dessert of galaktoboureko (custard pastry in syrup) with a glass of Muscat wine

day_by_day.notes: The Byzantine Museum is closed on Mondays – check current opening hours. The Venetian Castle is best visited in the late afternoon when the light is golden and temperatures cool slightly. Zakynthos Town is lively in the evenings – the waterfront fills with locals for the traditional evening volta (stroll).

day_by_day.morning: Early morning private speedboat excursion to the famous Marathonisi (Turtle Island) in the Gulf of Laganas – a protected nesting site for the endangered Loggerhead sea turtle (Caretta caretta). Swim in the pristine waters and, with luck, spot turtles surfacing near the boat. This is a UNESCO-protected marine park so guidelines must be respected.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Laganas Beach – one of Zakynthos's longest sandy beaches – for a premium beach club afternoon. Reserve a luxury sunbed setup with canopy, chilled towels, and bottle service. The calm, shallow waters here are ideal for swimming.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the boutique stay. Arrange a private chef experience at the hotel – a local Zakynthian chef prepares a traditional feast in your accommodation using market-fresh ingredients, explaining each dish as it is cooked.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast before the boat departure – Greek yogurt parfait, fresh fruit, and espresso
meals.lunch: Premium beach club lunch at Laganas – fresh seafood platter, watermelon and feta salad, and frozen cocktails
meals.dinner: Private chef dinner at the boutique stay – a curated 5-course Zakynthian menu featuring local rabbit stifado, stuffed zucchini flowers, handmade pasta with local truffle, and a dessert of mandola and local sweet wine

day_by_day.notes: Loggerhead turtle sightings are not guaranteed but are common in this marine park. Strictly no touching or feeding turtles – your licensed boat operator will brief you. Book the private chef experience at least 2 days in advance through the hotel concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely morning at the boutique stay – sleep in, enjoy a long breakfast, and spend time at the hotel's infinity pool or private terrace. This is a designated rest and recovery morning before the second half of the trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private wine and olive oil tasting tour of a traditional Zakynthian estate in the island's fertile interior. Zakynthos produces excellent local wines (Verdea, Muscat) and some of the finest olive oil in Greece. Tour the vineyards and olive groves, meet the producers, and taste multiple varieties paired with local bread and cheese.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in the picturesque village of Keri in the south of the island, perched above dramatic cliffs with views of the Mizithres rock formations rising from the sea. Watch the sunset from the Keri lighthouse viewpoint.

meals.breakfast: Extended luxury hotel breakfast – full spread including smoked salmon, eggs Benedict, fresh-squeezed juices, pastries, and Greek coffee
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the winery estate – charcuterie, artisan cheeses, marinated vegetables, and estate wine
meals.dinner: Dinner at a cliff-side taverna in Keri village – fresh grilled fish, local salads, and Keri's famous natural tar springs-inspired local lore over dessert and a digestif of Zakynthian kumquat liqueur

day_by_day.notes: Ask the hotel to arrange the winery visit in advance – several family estates near Machairado and Lagopodo offer private tastings for premium guests. The drive to Keri is approximately 30–40 minutes from Navagio area and the road is scenic through the island's green interior.

day_by_day.morning: Private ferry or speedboat transfer from Zakynthos to Kefalonia island (approximately 1.5–2 hours by ferry or 45 minutes by private speedboat). Check in at a luxury property in the Fiskardo area – the most glamorous village in the Ionian islands, with beautifully preserved Venetian architecture and a glittering yacht-filled harbor.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Fiskardo village on foot – browse the boutique shops, admire the pastel-colored Venetian buildings, and hire a small motorboat (no license required) to explore the hidden coves and sea caves along the Fiskardo peninsula independently.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner drinks at one of Fiskardo's elegant harbor-front bars, watching the superyachts drift in. The village transforms into a sophisticated social scene in the evenings.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: First lunch in Kefalonia at a harbor-front restaurant in Fiskardo – try Kefalonian meat pie (kreatopita), fresh lobster, and local Robola white wine
meals.dinner: Dinner at one of Fiskardo's premium restaurants – lobster spaghetti, grilled whole sea bass, and a dessert of Kefalonian honey pie with local thyme honey ice cream

day_by_day.notes: Book the inter-island transfer well in advance, especially for private speedboat options. Fiskardo is the most upscale village in the Ionians and attracts a sophisticated international crowd – reservations at top restaurants are essential in June. Pack a smaller overnight bag for the Kefalonia leg.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided boat tour from Fiskardo to the legendary Melissani Lake Cave – an otherworldly underground lake where sunlight pierces a collapsed roof to illuminate the water in vivid shades of blue and turquoise. Arrive early for the most magical light (around 11:00–12:00 when the sun is overhead). Also visit the nearby Drogarati stalactite cave.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive south to Myrtos Beach – consistently ranked among the most beautiful beaches in Europe, with dramatic white pebbles and intense turquoise water framed by towering white limestone cliffs. Arrange a premium beach setup through your hotel concierge.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Fiskardo for dinner. Stroll the harbor and enjoy the vibrant evening atmosphere of this chic village.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch on the boat or at a small café near Myrtos Beach – local pastries, fresh fruit, cold cuts, and chilled water
meals.dinner: Premium dinner at Fiskardo harbor – try Kefalonian-style moussaka, fresh grilled lobster, and a bottle of Gentilini Robola – one of Kefalonia's finest white wines

day_by_day.notes: Myrtos Beach has limited shade – bring a beach umbrella or arrange one through your hotel. The pebbles at Myrtos are large so water shoes are recommended. Melissani Cave is a must-see – the boat ride inside the cave is short but absolutely unforgettable. Arrive early to avoid midday crowds.

day_by_day.morning: Morning hike or private guided tour to the summit of Mount Ainos – the highest peak in the Ionian islands at 1,628 meters, covered in rare Kefalonian fir forest (Abies cephalonica). The national park offers cool, fragrant air and sweeping 360-degree views over multiple islands on a clear day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend and drive to Argostoli, Kefalonia's elegant capital. Visit the fascinating Korgialenios History and Folklore Museum, and stroll the lively Lithostroto pedestrian street. Stop at the Drapano Bridge causeway where loggerhead turtles are frequently spotted in the harbor channel.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Argostoli's lively restaurant district before returning to Fiskardo.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before the hike – energy-rich with eggs, whole grain bread, local honey, and Greek coffee
meals.lunch: Late lunch at a traditional kafeneion (coffee house) in a mountain village en route – local cheese pies, village salad, and cold mountain water
meals.dinner: Dinner in Argostoli – try the famous Kefalonian meat pie at a traditional restaurant, followed by fresh fish at a harbor-side taverna, with local Muscat dessert wine

day_by_day.notes: The Mount Ainos hike requires a moderate level of fitness and takes approximately 3–4 hours round trip. Wear proper hiking footwear and bring plenty of water. A private guide is strongly recommended for the best experience and safety. The temperature at the summit can be 8–10°C cooler than at sea level.

day_by_day.morning: Private speedboat or ferry transfer from Kefalonia (Fiskardo or Sami port) to Lefkada island – approximately 1.5–2 hours. Check in at a luxury boutique hotel near the famous Porto Katsiki or Egremni beach area on the west coast.
day_by_day.afternoon: First beach afternoon on Lefkada at the legendary Porto Katsiki – one of the most dramatic beaches in Greece, with towering white cliffs, fine white sand, and luminous blue water. Access via a long staircase from the clifftop parking area. Arrange a premium sunbed setup.
day_by_day.evening: Drive north to Lefkada Town for the evening – a charming town with distinctive earthquake-proof architecture (wooden upper floors, corrugated iron facades) and a lively waterfront promenade.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at a small taverna near Porto Katsiki or a picnic arranged by the hotel – fresh sandwiches, local pies, and cold drinks
meals.dinner: Dinner at a premium restaurant in Lefkada Town – try Lefkadian-style stuffed peppers, grilled fresh fish from the lagoon, and local wine from the Lefkada appellation

day_by_day.notes: Porto Katsiki can get crowded in the afternoon – aim to arrive by 14:00 or earlier. The staircase down to the beach is steep (approximately 100 steps) – wear appropriate footwear. Lefkada is connected to the mainland by a floating bridge, making it technically a peninsula – no ferry needed if arriving by land from the north.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the remote Egremni Beach – an even more secluded alternative to Porto Katsiki, accessible only by boat or via a very steep path (approximately 350 steps). Hire a private boat from the nearest small port for a VIP arrival directly onto the beach. The water here is among the clearest in the Mediterranean.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the beautiful inland village of Karya in Lefkada's mountainous interior – famous for its traditional embroidery and lace-making craft. Browse the artisan shops, visit the local folklore museum, and enjoy the cool mountain air under the enormous plane trees in the village square.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a clifftop bar on the west coast, then dinner back near the hotel or in a nearby village.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Lunch in Karya village at a traditional taverna under the plane trees – slow-cooked lamb kleftiko, village salad, local bread, and house wine
meals.dinner: Premium dinner at a beachside restaurant – fresh whole grilled fish, seafood risotto with local white wine, and a dessert of traditional ravani (semolina cake with syrup)

day_by_day.notes: The private boat to Egremni can be arranged through your hotel or at the small port of Athani. The boat journey takes approximately 10–15 minutes. Karya village is approximately 20–25 minutes from the coast by car – the road winds through beautiful mountain scenery.

day_by_day.morning: Indulgent final full morning – sleep in and enjoy a long, leisurely breakfast. Then a private luxury spa treatment at the hotel (massage, scrub, or hydrotherapy) to rejuvenate after days of activity. Many premium Lefkada properties have exceptional spa facilities.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final beach afternoon at Vasiliki Beach on the southern tip of Lefkada – a world-famous windsurfing and kitesurfing destination, but also a beautiful, calm bay perfect for swimming and relaxing. The bay is sheltered and the water is shallow and warm. Watch the colorful sails of windsurfers from your sunbed.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner – a truly special last evening in the Ionian islands. Choose the finest restaurant available near your hotel or arrange a private chef dinner on the beach or hotel terrace with a curated menu and premium wine selection.

meals.breakfast: Extended luxury breakfast – the full works, with everything the hotel offers, enjoyed slowly over coffee and fresh juice
meals.lunch: Light beach lunch at Vasiliki – fresh seafood, cold salads, and chilled local rosé wine
meals.dinner: Celebratory farewell dinner – a multi-course tasting menu featuring the best of Ionian cuisine: lobster, fresh fish, local cheeses, handmade pasta, and a dessert of loukoumades drizzled with thyme honey, paired with a premium bottle of Greek wine

day_by_day.notes: Book the spa treatment in advance. Vasiliki is approximately 30–35 minutes from the Porto Katsiki area by car. The farewell dinner reservation should be made at least 3–4 days in advance for the best tables. Consider a beach bonfire setup if the hotel can arrange it for a truly magical final evening.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning – a slow, peaceful breakfast with views of the Ionian Sea. Pack, check out, and take one last walk along the coast or clifftops to soak in the beauty of the Ionian islands.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private transfer to Aktion Airport (Preveza/Lefkada Airport) or, if returning via Zakynthos, arrange transfers accordingly. Depending on flight time, stop at a local bakery or deli to pick up Ionian food souvenirs – local honey, olive oil, Robola wine, kumquat liqueur, and traditional sweets.
day_by_day.evening: Departure – carry the flavors, colors, and warmth of the Ionian islands home.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast – enjoy every bite
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the airport or a nearby café before departure – Greek salad, a cheese pie, and a final Greek coffee
meals.dinner: In-flight or at destination

day_by_day.notes: Confirm all transfer timings the evening before. Allow extra time for check-out and the drive to the airport. Aktion Airport (PVK) serves Lefkada and is approximately 20–30 minutes away. If flying out of Zakynthos, factor in the inter-island transfer time of 2–3 hours. Greek customs allows generous quantities of olive oil and wine for personal use.

query: Greece under $2000, beaches and local food, summer 2026, flying from NYC
